title: Methane — Overview (Public edition)
description: Methane (CH4) is the simplest hydrocarbon: a tetrahedral molecule and the main component of natural gas. It is a potent short-lived greenhouse gas (roughly 80x CO2 over 20 years per unit mass) and the starting point of the entire petrochemical chain.
how_it_works: Read top-down: identity first, then structure, properties, reactions, and the deterministic scale chain. Each record derives from the molecule's parsed composition.

title: Methane — Identity and Composition
description: Methane is identified by the molecule CH4: CH4. Parsed deterministically, it contains C + H4 — 5 molecule(s), 10 protons and 10 electrons per molecule, molar mass 16.043 g/mol.
how_it_works: The build-time formula parser tokenizes the formula (handling parentheses and multipliers), looks up CIAAW 2021 atomic weights, and sums mass, atom, proton, and electron counts. The embedded demo re-derives the same numbers in JavaScript and fails the build if they differ.

title: Methane — Structure and Bonding
description: Perfect tetrahedron, H-C-H angle 109.5 degrees, C-H bond about 1.09 A. Nonpolar; very weak intermolecular forces, hence a gas with an extremely low boiling point.
how_it_works: Structure determines properties: geometry sets polarity, polarity sets solubility and boiling point, bonding sets reactivity. Read this record before the properties records.
